sections.heading: History
sections.text:
After the Organization's Suits attacked Lok Lambert and Sophie Casterwill at Lok's dormitory, Mindrone was sent to follow them. After DeFoe granted his Suits permission to use their Amulets, MacTavish's Mindrone stopped following Lok and attacked him, using its Mindzap ability while Lok was in a phone booth. When the Suits cornered Lok, Suit 001 instructed his Mindrone to attack but it was defeated by Dante Vale's Solwing. Elsewhere in the city, two more Mindrones were invoked by Suit 003 and Suit 004 to capture Sophie Casterwill for interrogation. These Mindrones, however, were defeated offscreen by Sophie and Santiago. [A Seeker Is Born]

Charlene Hubbs invoked her Mindrone at the Golem's Attic to attack Lok Lambert but it was defeated by his Freelancer. [Words of Truth, Heart of Lies]

DeFoe invoked his own Mindrone to attack Dante Vale alongside Gar-Ghoul in the hull of the shipwreck. After being overpowered, DeFoe was forced to admit defeat and his Mindrone retreated. [The Treasures of the Argonauts]

Ford's Mindrone fought alongside Caliban against Lee Roy's Enforcer and a pair of Redcap Titans. [The Titan of the Stage]

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext: Mindrone enjoys making others suffer. {{Source|TCG:SAS-042|SAS-042}} His Mindzap ability creates optical laser blasts which can burn or knock a weak opponent unconscious. Like insects, Mindrone Titans also have the ability to adhere to surfaces, clinging to them to travel or to ambush a target, nimbly moving across city walls. In addition, they can levitate in the air. {{source|A Seeker Is Born}} Its two enormous stingers can also inject a deadly poison. {{source|Huntik Magazine}} With its bionic eye, Mindrone is also able to transmit visual information to his Seeker's [[Tome]], and due its silent nature, these Titans make great spies. {{source|Absent Heroes}}

full_text:
Mindrone is a bipedal Swara-Titan with a prominent, single red eye taking the place of its face and two wiry appendages protruding from its back. Mindrone is related to the power-equivalent Terrapede Titans and to the weaker Enforcer Titans. As this sadistic Titan enjoys making people suffer, Mindrone as well as its related Titans are commonly used by the Suits of the evil Organization for both combat and as spies.

History

After the Organization's Suits attacked Lok Lambert and Sophie Casterwill at Lok's dormitory, Mindrone was sent to follow them. After DeFoe granted his Suits permission to use their Amulets, MacTavish's Mindrone stopped following Lok and attacked him, using its Mindzap ability while Lok was in a phone booth. When the Suits cornered Lok, Suit 001 instructed his Mindrone to attack but it was defeated by Dante Vale's Solwing. Elsewhere in the city, two more Mindrones were invoked by Suit 003 and Suit 004 to capture Sophie Casterwill for interrogation. These Mindrones, however, were defeated offscreen by Sophie and Santiago. [A Seeker Is Born]

Charlene Hubbs invoked her Mindrone at the Golem's Attic to attack Lok Lambert but it was defeated by his Freelancer. [Words of Truth, Heart of Lies]

DeFoe invoked his own Mindrone to attack Dante Vale alongside Gar-Ghoul in the hull of the shipwreck. After being overpowered, DeFoe was forced to admit defeat and his Mindrone retreated. [The Treasures of the Argonauts]

Ford's Mindrone fought alongside Caliban against Lee Roy's Enforcer and a pair of Redcap Titans. [The Titan of the Stage]

Abilities

Mindrone enjoys making others suffer. [SAS-042] His Mindzap ability creates optical laser blasts which can burn or knock a weak opponent unconscious. Like insects, Mindrone Titans also have the ability to adhere to surfaces, clinging to them to travel or to ambush a target, nimbly moving across city walls. In addition, they can levitate in the air. [A Seeker Is Born] Its two enormous stingers can also inject a deadly poison. [Huntik Magazine] With its bionic eye, Mindrone is also able to transmit visual information to his Seeker's Tome, and due its silent nature, these Titans make great spies. [Absent Heroes]
